In [[mathematics]], the '''Gieseking manifold''' is a cusped [[hyperbolic 3-manifold]] of finite volume, discovered by Hugo Gieseking.{{sfnp|Gieseking|1912}} It is [[orientability|non-orientable]] and has the smallest volume among non-compact hyperbolic manifolds, having volume approximately <math>V \approx 1.0149416</math>.

The Gieseking manifold can be constructed by removing the vertices from a [[tetrahedron]], then gluing the faces together in pairs using affine-linear maps.  Label the vertices 0, 1, 2, 3.  Glue the face with vertices 0, 1, 2 to the face with vertices 3, 1, 0 in that order.  Glue the face 0, 2, 3 to the face 3, 2, 1 in that order. In the hyperbolic structure of the Gieseking manifold, this ideal tetrahedron is the canonical polyhedral decomposition of [[David B. A. Epstein]] and Robert C. Penner.  Moreover, the angle made by the faces is <math>\pi/3</math>.  The triangulation has one tetrahedron, two faces, one edge and no vertices, so all the edges of the original tetrahedron are glued together.

The Gieseking manifold has a [[covering space|double cover]] [[homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] to the [[figure-eight knot (mathematics)|figure-eight knot]] [[knot complement|complement]].  The underlying compact manifold has a [[Klein bottle]] boundary, and the first [[homology group]] of the Gieseking manifold is the integers.

The Gieseking manifold is a fiber bundle over the circle with fiber the [[once-punctured]] torus and monodromy given by <math>(x,y) \to (x+y,x).</math>
The square of this map is [[Arnold's cat map]] and this gives another way to see that the Gieseking manifold is double covered by the complement of the figure-eight knot.

==Gieseking constant==
The volume of the Gieseking manifold is called the [[:de:Gieseking-Konstante|Gieseking constant]] and has a numeral value of

: <math>V = \operatorname{Cl}_2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 1.01494 \ 16064 \ 09653 \ 62502 \ 12025 \dots</math> {{OEIS|A143298}}
where <math>\operatorname{Cl}_2</math> is the [[Clausen function]].<ref>{{MathWorld|id=GiesekingsConstant|title=Gieseking's constant}}</ref> This is similar to [[Catalan's constant]] <math>G</math>, which also manifests as a volume and can be expressed in terms of the Clausen function:

:<math>G=\operatorname{Cl}_2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0.91596559\dots</math>

There is a related expression in terms of a special value of a [[Dirichlet L-function|Dirichlet ''L''-function]] given by the identity{{sfnp|Finch|2003|pp=232–233}}

:<math>V = \frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{4} \cdot L(2,\chi_{-3}) = \frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{4} \bigg(\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(3k+1)^2} - \frac{1}{(3k+2)^2}\bigg),</math>

whereas [[Catalan's constant]] is equal to <math>L(2,\chi_{-4})</math>. It follows that

:<math>\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(3k+1)^2}=\frac{2\pi^2}{27}+\frac{2\sqrt3}{9}V,</math>

:<math>\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(3k+2)^2}=\frac{2\pi^2}{27}-\frac{2\sqrt3}{9}V.</math>

Catalan's constant satisfies similar equations:

:<math>\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(4k+1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{16}+\frac{1}{2}G,</math>

:<math>\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(4k+3)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{16}-\frac{1}{2}G.</math>

Another closed form expression may be given in terms of the [[trigamma function]]:

:<math>V = \frac{\sqrt 3}{3}\left(\frac{\psi_1(1/3)}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{3}\right).</math>

Integrals for the Gieseking constant are given by

:<math>V = \int_{0}^{2\pi/3} \ln\left(2\cos\left(\tfrac12x\right)\right)\mathrm dx = 2\int_0^1 \frac{\ln(1+x)}{\sqrt{(1-x)(3+x)}}\mathrm dx</math>

which follow from its definition with the Clausen function and{{sfnp|Bailey|Borwein|Crandall|2006}}

:<math>V =\frac{\sqrt{3}}2 \int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty \frac{\mathrm{d}x \ \mathrm{d}y \ \mathrm dz}{xyz (x+y+z+\tfrac1x+\tfrac1y+\tfrac1z)^2}.</math>

In 2024, [[Frank Calegari]], [[Vesselin Dimitrov]], and [[Yunqing Tang]] proved that <math>1, \pi^2, L(2,\chi_{-3})</math>  are linearly independent over the rationals. This proves that <math>\sqrt{3} \cdot V</math> is irrational as well as the special values <math>\psi_1(1/6)</math>, <math>\psi_1(1/3)</math>, <math>\psi_1(2/3)</math>, <math>\psi_1(5/6)</math> of the trigamma function. The irrationality of <math>V</math> itself is still open.<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=2408.15403 |last1=Calegari |first1=Frank |author1-link=Frank Calegari |last2=Dimitrov |first2=Vesselin |author2-link=Vesselin Dimitrov |last3=Tang |first3=Yunqing |author3-link=Yunqing Tang |title=The linear independence of 1, ''ζ''(2), and ''L''(2,''χ''<sub>-3</sub>) |year=2024 |class=math.NT }}</ref>
